To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cohesive forces are needed to prevent the rotational breakup and mass shedding of a rubble-pile asteroid and that these forces are comparable in strength to the van der Waals force between lunar regolith grains.
(i) the asteroid (29075 1950 Da) rotates faster than is allowed purely by gravity and friction and (ii) cohesive forces are needed to prevent its surface mass shedding and its structural failure.

the asteroid (29075)(1950) DA is a rubble pile rotating faster than is permitted by gravity and friction, and that cohesive forces are necessary to prevent surface mass-shedding and structural failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical behaviour of asteroids.
the physical behaviour of rubble-pile asteroids, and in particular the cohesive forces between constituent grains.
the physical behaviour of rubble-pile asteroids and the role of small-scale cohesive forces in the evolution of these bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cohesive forces are important for small rubble-pile asteroids.
the cohesion of rubble pile asteroids is a significant factor in their dynamics.
cohesive forces are important, but not dominant, in the stability and dynamics of rubble-pile asteroids, and that their effects are most important at small asteroid sizes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asteroid 1950 DA is a rubble pile, that it is spinning faster than gravity and friction can explain and that it is spinning so fast that the cohesive forces are important.
cohesive forces in the form van der Waals interactions are required to explain the observed rotational behaviour of 29075 DA.
cohesive forces are important and can prevent the rotational breakup for some asteroids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cohesive strength of a rubble pile is not a simple function of the size of its constituent grains.
cohesive forces can prevent the breakup of small asteroids.
cohesive forces are likely to play a significant role in the rotational dynamics of rubble-pile asteroids.
